current_bottleneck: 280a showed that learned residual scaling is the right Stage B mechanism class, but one scalar per query is too blunt. It improves global coverage and jump-scale metrics, but flattens regime differentiation and still leaves full-horizon mean_reversion below gate. The live bottleneck is now horizon-structured residual scaling without moving the fixed 277d Stage A center path.
last_result_summary: Iteration 90 ran 280a-v0 and scored 4/11. It improved overall coverage to 72.3%, pushed h30 coverage through gate, improved coverage floor, kurtosis ratio, and jump KS, but regime differentiation collapsed toward 1.0 and mean_reversion still failed on the full-horizon profile. Iteration 91 then selected 280b-v0 as the next clean step: a minimal query-conditioned horizon-scale profile over the same fixed residual bank.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 280b-v0: center-preserving hierarchical retrieval with 4 learned horizon-anchor scales interpolated across the 30-day horizon.
current_best_model: 277d-v0 and 279a-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 277d is the strongest deterministic Stage A core; 279a is the strongest explicit two-level hierarchical model so far. The next step is to interpolate between 278a's spread and 279a's center preservation.
